newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK's Abbey eyes Cater operations.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK's Abbey eyes Cater operations.

text.p: British bank Abbey National Plc on Monday confirmed it was in bid talks with financial services group Cater Allen Holdings Plc, and analysts said Cater's offshore and retail operations would fit neatly with Abbey's business.

"Abbey National plc confirms that it is in talks with Cater Allen Holdings plc which may lead to an offer for that company. A further announcement will be made in due course," Abbey National said in a statement.
Cater had its origins as a discount house dealing with the Bank of England, and is still active in its traditional money market activities.
But in common with other houses, has found it difficult to turn a profit in those markets, and has sold its futures trading operations.
Instead, it has diversified into onshore banking, where deposits are growing, and particularly offshore -- where it has profitable operations in Jersey and the Isle of Man.
These would fit in well with Abbey which, in addition to those two centres, also has operations in Gibraltar and Hong Kong.

Another Cater business which may have attracted Abbey is its presence in the retail share dealing market, where it owns City Deal and a few months ago added Glasgow-based stockbroker Aitken Campbell which runs its own electronic share dealing service.
Abbey itself has also been busily diversifying away from its traditional savings and mortgages operations.
"Anything that continues Abbey's strategy to move away from the mortgage business is to be welcomed," said one analyst, "although this is quite a small step."

Abbey, formerly a mutual building society that floated on the stock exchange in 1989, has said it wants to reduce its dependence on the highly competitive savings and mortgage areas from which it still derives some 60 percent of earnings.
In 1996, Abbey raised its profit in treasury and offshore business by 18 percent to 256 million pounds, before integration costs, and grew assets by 14 percent to 47.8 billion.

Abbey refused to comment on the bid talks but analysts said a price of 200 million pounds ($327 million) was likely for Cater which, at Monday's share price of 547.5p per share is capitalised at around 170 million pounds.
Cater Allen shares surged about 25 percent on June 5, when it said it was in talks that could lead to an offer. But on Monday they stood 2.5p lower after the Abbey announcement.
Various groups have been mentioned as potential bidders for Cater but Abbey is thought to want to add the company to its well developed Treasury division.
Abbey, whose shares were down 26p to 869-1/2p in a generally lower banking sector, was recently linked to UK banking giant National Westminster Bank Plc.
Earlier this month, Abbey confirmed that it had held discussions with NatWest, but that these had been terminated. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
